MINUTES

  SPECIAL MEETING
  GLENDALE TRANSPORTATION & PARKING COMMISSION
  March 25, 2019

The regular meeting of the Glendale Transportation & Parking Commission (TPC) of Monday,
March 25, 2019 was called to order at 6:04 p.m.

1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 6:04 p.m. Chairperson Kurkjian called the meeting to order.
  a. Roll Call –Yacoubian, Chairperson Kurkjian, Nazarian
  Absent: Gonzalez, Sahakian
  b. Flag Salute – Chairperson Kurkjian

2. POSTING OF AGENDA
  The agenda for the Monday, March 25, 2019 Regular Meeting of the Glendale
  Transportation & Parking Commission was posted by Friday, March 22, 2019 before 5:00
  p.m. on the bulletin board outside of City Hall.

3. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five
  minutes. The Commission may question the speaker but there will be no debate or
  decision.
  There were no speakers at this time.

4. INFORMATION ONLY
  a. Los Angeles-Glendale-Burbank Feasibility Study

Assistant Director of Public Works, Edward Hitti, introduced Mr. Jay Fuhrman from Metro, who
presented on the Los Angeles-Glendale-Burbank Feasibility Study. Mr. Fuhrman briefly described
the study as a planning feasibility analysis of the corridor between Los Angeles, Glendale and
Burbank with an emphasis on three main ideas: to provide more frequent services to the
community, to study the growth in population in the surrounding areas, and to relieve congestion.
Mr. Fuhrman introduced his colleague, Jeannette Owens, who elaborated on the five options Metro
developed to fulfill these goals, one of which was adding a new Metrolink station on either
Grandview Avenue, or Sonora Avenue. In closing, Ms. Owens informed the Commission that
Metro is currently meeting with stakeholders, gathering more ridership information, and would be
finalizing their report soon, after which they will be presenting their findings to the Metro Board for
approval in the fall of this year.

Commissioner Yacoubian expressed her main concern as lack of ridership and also asked how
this new station may affect the quiet zone in the neighboring areas. Ms. Owens acknowledged
these concerns and explained that they are still looking into ridership numbers and in addition,
would extra measures to maintain the existing quiet zones. Chairperson Kurkjian asked why Metro
would consider placing a station at San Fernando Road and Sonora Avenue, rather than
Grandview Avenue. Ms. Owens mentioned that the station at Sonora Avenue would service the
staff in the Dreamworks and Disney studios more directly and would also be using their property to
place the Metro platforms rather than buying right of way areas.

Mr. Hitti mentioned he would follow up on this concept and meet with the traffic engineering staff
and the film studios to get an update. Ms. Owens ultimately said Metro will place a station
wherever the City of Glendale would prefer.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING
  a. Proposed Preferential Parking for the 300 block of Lafayette Street between Colorado
  Street and Dixon Street.
  (1a). Resolution to approve the establishment of a “2 Hour, 9am to 6pm, Monday to Friday,
  Except by Permit’ parking restriction on the 300 block of Lafayette Street, between
  Colorado Street and Dixon Street.

Mr. Tad Dombroski from the Parking division for City of Glendale, Public Works department
presented this item. Mr. Dombroski explained that there are three main things that affect the
parking situation for residents that live at the 300 block of Lafayette Street including an autobody
shop, a hotel business and a neighboring school. Patrons from these three agencies have created
an shortage of parking space for residents.

Mrs. Hortensia Martinez who lives on 312 ½ Lafayette Street expressed her concerns for the lack
of parking space on her street to the extreme that she feels she cannot drive her own vehicle late
at night to check on her sick elderly mother, for fear of not having a parking space when she
returned. She was in favor of the resolution for preferential parking.

Naira Zohrabyan who lives at 319 Lafayette Street, and Cristina Diaz of 313 ½ Lafayette Street
also spoke about their hardship with the lack of parking on their street and expressed that they
were in favor of the resolution for preferential parking.

Moved: Yacoubian  Second: Nazarian
Roll Call: Yacoubian, Nazarian, Chairperson Kurkjian
Absent: Gonzalez, Sahakian

  b. Proposed Preferential Parking for the 1500 block of Lynglen Drive to East Glenoaks
  Boulevard.
  (1b). Resolution to approve the establishment of a “2 Hour, 9am to 6pm, Monday to Friday,
  Except by Permit’ parking restriction on the 1500 block of Lynglen Drive, from 1500 Lynglen
  Drive to East Glenoaks Boulevard.

Mr. Tad Dombroski presented this item. He explained that the employees at a medical office
located on Chevy Chase Drive have created a severe parking shortage for residents who live on
the 1500 block of Lynglen Drive. Four community members from different residences appeared in
support of this resolution to implement preferential parking on their street: Sandra Bayz from 1574
LynGlen Drive, Hripsime Bagdasanyan of 1525 Lynglen Drive, Jim Tarouilly of 1574 Lynglen Drive
and Alex Semeujian of 1522 Lynglen Drive. Some of the resounding concerns of the residents
were a lack of parking for residents, a buildup of trash on the street, and a concern for a potential
decrease in property value.

Moved: Yacoubian  Second: Nazarian
Roll Call: Yacoubian, Chairperson Kurkjian, Nazarian
Absent: Gonzalez, Sahakian

 6. ACTION ITEM
  a. Installation of Speed Humps on Geneva Street between Doran Street and Lexington
  Avenue

Mr. Pastor Casanova, a traffic engineer for the City of Glendale, presented this item. Mr. Casanova
requested to move forward with installing speed humps on Geneva Street to reduce speeding near
R.D. White Elementary School. Mr. Casanova explained that the engineering assessment of
Geneva Street showed that the street’s conditions met the criteria to implement the speed humps
for the following reasons: Geneva Street is a local street, is located in a residential area and is in a
school zone. Mr. Casanova collected a petition from 34 of the 40 residents on the block, rendering
an 85% show of support from local residents.

Moved: Yacoubian  Second: Nazarian
Roll Call: Yacoubian, Chairperson Kurkjian, Nazarian
Absent: Gonzalez, Sahakian

8. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS/UPDATES

Mr. Larry Tay from the Engineering division of the Public Works department provided an update on
the Commission’s previous request to extend the guardrail on the 2 freeway onramp at Mountain
Street. This request was denied by Caltrans. Commissioner Yacoubian asked Senior Assistant
City Attorney, Miah Yun, if the City would be protected from any legal repercussions should any
accident occur on that onramp since the guardrail would not be extended. Mrs. Yun replied that as
a City, we are protected because we had put Caltrans on notice of this safety hazard.

In addition, Mr. Tay explained the reason for the operation restriction on the right turn lane on
Mountain Street by the 2 freeway onramp was due to the request and petitioning of the San Rafael
Home Owner’s Association. Before the restriction was in effect, residents coming from the east
side of Mountain were not able to make a left turn onto the southbound 2 freeway because of the
heavy traffic coming from the opposite side of the street. It was mentioned that perhaps the timing
of the restricted operation could be adjusted depending on peak hours to offer some relief for both
sides of traffic. Mr. Tay said Caltrans agreed to meet with the City’s engineering staff for a field
meeting in hopes of changing the timing parameters.

Mr. Hitti gave updates on the three Engineering projects: Pennsylvania Avenue Rehabilitation
Project, the Highland Avenue Rehabilitation Project and the Verdugo Boulevard Rehabilitation
Project.

In conclusion, Commissioner Yacoubian mentioned the median along Glendale Avenue leading up
to Glendale City College needed to be better maintained by City staff as it is in a high traffic area
seen by many visitors and residents alike. Mr. Hitti acknowledged this concern and agreed to work
with staff both in Public Works and the Parks and Recreation department to take better care of this
area.

6. ADJOURNMENT: 8:45 p.m.

Moved: Yacoubian  Second: Nazarian
